delights: It admitted when it could not hit my numbers instead of quietly missing: "Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance - closest was \"Turkey & Swiss Roll-Ups\" (landed 168 kcal vs a 136 target)." I trust a tool more when it says that out loud.

The alternates were instant and genuinely appetising - "High-Protein White Fish & Onions with Rice" at matchPct 100, and "Bangladeshi fish curry with daikon" (daikon, turmeric, green chilli, coriander leaves, lime) also at 100. That is the first thing all day I actually wanted to eat.

Not one of my 17 ingredients broke a wall: no gluten grain, no soy, no beef, no sesame. The one dish tagged cuisine "asian" carried no soy sauce at all, and my starches were rice, quinoa and potato - all naturally safe for a coeliac.

defects.what: Three of my five meals were built on a vegan egg substitute while my diet is set to "none" - and the dish title claims real eggs, so nothing warns you
defects.snippet: "Classic Eggs & Broccoli with Potato" - ingredients: 215 g "flax eggs"

defects.what: The day put 420 g of flax eggs in front of me even after I swapped one slot out; flax is a laxative in ~30 g doses, so this is a genuine digestive hazard for a man working fire shifts

The flax-eggs macros are arithmetically impossible, so I cannot trust the protein total that my whole high-protein goal rests on - the slot reports 10.5 g fat while containing 10 g of olive oil, leaving roughly 0 g of fat for 215 g of a seed that is about 42% fat (those look like egg-white numbers on a flax row)
defects.snippet: 215 g flax eggs + 160 g Russet Potato + 100 g Broccoli + 10 g Olive Oil -> "fat": 10.5

defects.what: The shopping list itself cannot tell whether flax eggs are eggs - it sends me to buy a dozen eggs for them
Two of my three snacks are the identical dish on the same day
defects.snippet: snack slot 1 and snack slot 2 are both "Greek Yogurt, Honey & Almonds" (85 g Greek Yogurt, 8 g Almonds, 5 g Honey)

defects.what: The swap endpoint rejects the recipeId it had just offered me one call earlier, with an error about a problem I did not cause; it only worked when I resent the entire alternate object including its ingredient array
defects.snippet: PUT .../slots/.../apply with {"recipeId":"cmrul4e6v006owl6849588n2z"} -> 400 {"error":"a slot needs at least one ingredient"}

defects.what: Customer-facing text tells me, the user, to go edit a source code file
defects.snippet: "rough manually-entered CAD estimate, not sourced pricing data - edit src/lib/groceryPrices.js to correct"

defects.what: These are not recipes - the entire method for a main meal is two short sentences, and "cook" makes no sense for a flax slurry
defects.snippet: steps: ["Cook the eggs.", "Serve with potato and bell peppers."]

defects.what: Prepackaged deli luncheon meat is the one item on this plan a coeliac who also avoids soy has to label-check, because binders in that category routinely carry wheat starch and soy protein - the plan picks it twice and never flags it, where plain roast turkey breast would have been safe
defects.snippet: "Turkey breast, low salt, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat" - 100 g in a meal plus 55 g in a snack

defects.what: The shopping quantities are in cooked/as-prepared weight, which I cannot buy - honest about it, but it leaves me doing the dry-weight conversion myself
defects.snippet: "White rice, cooked  pantry  225g" with form "as-prepared (state unrecorded) - NOT a raw/dry purchase quantity"

followUp.action: Asked for alternates on the breakfast slot because I did not want 160 g of flax eggs, then swapped in the white fish option
followUp.howItWent: The alternates call was the best moment of the session - three options in one shot, two at 100% match, all safe for my walls, including a real spiced fish curry. The swap then failed with 400 "a slot needs at least one ingredient" when I sent just the recipeId it had given me, and only went through when I resent the whole alternate object; after that the plan re-read correctly with White Fish in place and the day still landed at 2,154 kcal against my 2,129 target.

verdict: My allergies and my coeliac disease were respected and the day hits 2,154 kcal against a 2,129 target with 174 g of protein, but three of five meals were a vegan flax egg substitute mislabelled as "Classic Eggs" with fat numbers that cannot be true, my snack repeated verbatim, and the only food I actually wanted was an alternate I had to hunt down myself.
